sentences.text: Crossvallia is an extinct genus of penguins belonging to the family Spheniscidae.
This genus includes two species: C. unienwillia and the questionably placed ?C. waiparensis.
Anatomical evidence suggests that Crossvallia is closely related to the subfamily Anthropornithinae.
C. waiparensis was significantly larger than the largest living penguin species, the Emperor penguin, which reaches about 121.9 cm and weighs up to 36 kg.
The species C. unienwillia measured approximately 140 cm in length.
The species C. unienwillia was the first described in the genus, named after the Late Paleocene Cross Valley Formation on Seymour Island, Antarctica.
The species C. waiparensis was described in August 2019 based on leg bone fossils found in Waipara, New Zealand, discovered by amateur paleontologist Leigh Love.

Crossvallia is thought to have lived during the final stages of the Cretaceous and the Paleocene, between 66 and 56 million years ago, specifically from the Selandian to the Thanetian stages, spanning 61.66 to 56 million years ago.
